overview.historicalContext:
This proof is attributed to Hippasus of Metapontum (~500 BCE), a member of the Pythagorean school who discovered that the diagonal of a unit square cannot be expressed as a ratio of integers. According to legend, Hippasus was thrown overboard while at sea for revealing this truth, which shook the Pythagorean doctrine that 'all is number' — meaning rational number.

The Greeks called such lengths *incommensurable* with the side: no common unit of measurement can divide both exactly. The result appears formally in Euclid's *Elements* Book X (c. 300 BCE). Theaetetus (~400 BCE) extended it, proving √n is irrational for any non-perfect-square n.

The proof exemplifies *infinite descent*: assuming √2 = a/b in lowest terms forces both a and b to be even, contradicting 'lowest terms'. This parity argument became a template replicated across number theory — the same structure proves √p irrational for any prime p.
overview.problemStatement:
**Theorem**: There are no natural numbers a, b with b > 0 such that a^2 = 2 * b^2 and gcd(a,b) = 1.

This is equivalent to saying sqrt(2) is irrational, since if sqrt(2) = a/b in lowest terms, then a^2 = 2b^2.
overview.text: A complete proof that sqrt(2) is irrational built from first principles, demonstrating the classical proof by contradiction with even/odd analysis.
overview.proofStrategy:
**The Classic Proof by Contradiction**:

1. Assume sqrt(2) = a/b where a, b are coprime
2. Then 2b^2 = a^2, so a^2 is even
3. Therefore a is even (key lemma!), say a = 2k
4. Substituting: 2b^2 = 4k^2, so b^2 = 2k^2
5. Therefore b^2 is even, so b is even
6. But both a and b even contradicts gcd(a,b) = 1!
keyInsights: The key lemma is: if n^2 is even, then n is even — proved by contrapositive: if n is odd (n = 2k+1), then n² = 4k² + 4k + 1 is also odd, so the implication holds by contraposition
Even/odd definitions and all parity lemmas are built from scratch using only existential witnesses, showing the full proof architecture hidden inside Mathlib's one-liner `exact irrational_sqrt_two`

The proof uses infinite descent implicitly: assuming a/b in lowest terms leads to 2|a and 2|b, so a/2 and b/2 give a 'smaller' representation — repeating this descent has no finite stopping point unless no such a/b exists

The contrapositive technique generalizes directly to √p for any prime p: replace 'divisible by 2' with 'divisible by p', and the same argument shows p|a² → p|a (using the prime property), then p|b — contradiction with coprimality

This ~200-line pedagogical proof illustrates the trade-off in formalization: Mathlib's one-liner `exact irrational_sqrt_two` hides real number construction, the square root definition, and the actual irrationality argument — this file makes all of that structure explicit
prerequisites: Axiomatic real analysis (ordered field axioms, completeness)

sections.title: Basic Definitions
sections.summary: Defining even and odd numbers from scratch.
sections.mathContext: Defines even ($\exists k, n = 2k$) and odd ($\exists k, n = 2k+1$) from scratch, without importing Mathlib. A self-contained development from first principles.

sections.title: Parity Lemmas
sections.summary: Every number is even XOR odd; successor flips parity.
sections.mathContext: Every natural number is even XOR odd. Successor flips parity: $n$ even $\iff$ $n+1$ odd. Proved by induction on $n$.

sections.title: Key Lemma: Even Squares
sections.summary: If n^2 is even, then n is even (proved by contrapositive).
sections.mathContext: The key lemma: $n^2$ even $\Rightarrow n$ even. Proved by contrapositive: $n$ odd $\Rightarrow n = 2k+1 \Rightarrow n^2 = 4k^2+4k+1$ odd.

sections.title: The Main Theorem
sections.summary: No coprime solution to a^2 = 2b^2 exists.
sections.mathContext: The main result: no coprime integers $a, b$ satisfy $a^2 = 2b^2$. Proof: $a^2 = 2b^2 \Rightarrow a^2$ even $\Rightarrow a$ even $\Rightarrow a = 2c \Rightarrow 4c^2 = 2b^2 \Rightarrow b^2$ even $\Rightarrow b$ even, contradicting coprimality.

crossReferences.description: The standard formalization of $\sqrt{2}$ irrationality using Mathlib — this entry proves the same result from first principles without Mathlib, making every axiom explicit

Both are classical number-theoretic results proved from basic properties of integers — the infinitude of primes and irrationality of $\sqrt{2}$ are the foundational examples of proof by contradiction in number theory
The well-ordering principle (equivalent to induction) underpins the infinite descent argument used in the classic proof of $\sqrt{2}$'s irrationality
The GCD algorithm and the notion of coprimality ($\gcd(p,q)=1$) are central to the standard proof: if $p^2 = 2q^2$ with $\gcd(p,q)=1$, then both $p$ and $q$ must be even, contradicting coprimality
Companion entry providing concrete computational examples of $\sqrt{2}$ approximations and decimal expansions, complementing this axiomatic irrationality proof
Generalizes the $\sqrt{2}$ irrationality proof to $\sqrt[n]{m}$ for non-perfect-$n$th-powers $m$ — the same parity/divisibility argument extends using unique prime factorization

The fundamental theorem of arithmetic (unique prime factorization) provides the deeper reason the proof works: $p^2 = 2q^2$ forces $2$ to appear an odd number of times on the right, contradicting the even exponent on the left

The Pythagorean theorem $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ on a unit right triangle gives $c = \sqrt{2}$, the original geometric motivation for studying its irrationality — Hippasus discovered incommensurability through this diagonal

Both $\sqrt{2}$ (irrational but algebraic) and $\pi$ (transcendental) lie outside $\mathbb{Q}$, but $\pi$'s transcendence is far stronger — comparing these proofs illustrates the hierarchy: rational $\subset$ algebraic $\subset$ real
